title: What is the units digit of this huge division?
description: A very large division of powers of two is solved by writing four as two squared and cancelling twos, the same way as the halving line. The units digit then comes from the repeating pattern of the powers of two.
teaching_notes: One idea: write every power with the same base, take the exponents away, and use the repeating units digits of powers of two. Watch for students who try to work out the huge number, or who divide the exponents.

video_script.why: A learner uses the same-base cancelling of the halving line on large powers, and then finds the units digit from a repeating pattern.
video_script.substitution: the book's own division of two to the power two hundred and twenty four by four to the power thirty two
video_script.anchor: two to the power two hundred and twenty four divided by four to the power thirty two, written as a fraction
video_script.payoff_line: The units digit of the value is six
maths_rules: units digits of 2^1, 2^2, 2^3, 2^4 are 2, 4, 8, 6 and then repeat
2^160 ends in the same digit as 2^4 = 16, which is 6
video_script.design: One idea: same base, take the exponents away, then use the units digit cycle. The cycle is drawn as four steps round a loop and the digit only appears at the answer.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='take'/>Take two to the power two hundred and twenty four.
<bookmark mark='divide'/>Divide it by four to the power thirty two.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What is the units digit of the result? The book gives a hint, that four is two squared.

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>We solve this the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='base'/>Write both powers with the same base, and then cancel.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, two to the power two hundred and twenty four divided by four to the power thirty two. Also, four is two squared.

beats.on_screen: To find: the units digit of the value

marks.find: the words units digit of the value are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the units digit of the value.

marks.mul: 2 x 32 is written in the exponent

narration: <bookmark mark='swap'/>Step one, write four as two squared, so that both powers have the base two.
<bookmark mark='mul'/>Thirty two groups of two twos make two times thirty two twos.
<bookmark mark='base'/>Four to the power thirty two is then two to the power sixty four.
<bookmark mark='frac'/>Step two, divide with the same base, because the twos below cancel twos above.
<bookmark mark='take'/>Two hundred and twenty four take away sixty four is one hundred and sixty.
<bookmark mark='res'/>The value is two to the power one hundred and sixty.

beats.on_screen: units digits of 2^1, 2^2, 2^3, 2^4, 2^5: 2, 4, 8, 6, 2, and the pattern repeats in fours

marks.list: 2^1 = 2, 2^2 = 4, 2^3 = 8, 2^4 = 16 are written with their units digits circled
marks.again: 2^5 = 32 starts the same digits again, and a loop of four is drawn

narration: <bookmark mark='list'/>Step three, look at the units digits of the powers of two. They go two, four, eight, six.
<bookmark mark='again'/>The next power starts the same four digits again, so the pattern repeats after every four powers.

beats.on_screen: 160 / 4 = 40: 160 is a multiple of 4, so it sits at the last place of the loop

marks.place: 2^160 is placed at the last step of the loop

narration: <bookmark mark='div'/>Step four, see where one hundred and sixty falls. One hundred and sixty divided by four is exactly forty.
<bookmark mark='place'/>It is a multiple of four, so it lands on the last place of the pattern.

beats.on_screen: check: 2^8 = 256 and 2^4 = 16 have the same units digit

marks.same: the units digits of both are circled in the same colour

narration: <bookmark mark='small'/>Step five, check the pattern on a small power. Two to the power eight is two hundred and fifty six.
<bookmark mark='same'/>Eight is a multiple of four. Its units digit matches two to the power four, which is sixteen.

marks.pay: the units place of 2^160 is boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>The units digit of the value is six.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Two to the power one hundred and sixty ends in six.
